messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1767777000 - us-east-1b partial networking + host-level connection resets impacting inference-serving. Trigger: synthetic canaries + customer error spikes. Initial severity P2 -> escalated to P1.

maya: seeing a sudden jump in TCP RST counts from g5-inference-node pool in us-east-1b, started ~03:01 UTC. p50 normal but p95 and error rate up.

sre-marc: confirmed. KVS cache miss rate also spiked, looks like a mix of packet drops and some hosts dropping connections mid-stream.

eng-runtime-sara: pulling logs now, streaming a tail of /var/log/syslog on affected host:

```
Mar 15 03:02:12 host-123 kernel: TCP: Unexpected RST from 10.0.45.12:443 -> closing socket
Mar 15 03:02:13 host-123 kubelet: eviction signal: net_unavailable
```

maya: can we quickly divert traffic from us-east-1b to us-east-2 for the inference-route? pref failover?

infra-joe: starting controlled diversion: creating additional target group in us-east-2 and will update routing policy. Note: cold KV caches in us-east-2 will increase token cost/temp latency.

support-anais: customer impact snapshot: between 03:00-03:10 UTC hosted-api had 14% 5xx rate globally, but us-east-1b origins show ~32% 502/504. Affected customers: several small PLG apps; no enterprise SLAs breached yet but we should notify larger accounts proactively.

eng-runtime-sara: running health-check against the inference-serving path from a probe inside us-east-1b: `curl -v https://inference.internal/api/health` -> intermittent ECONNRESET.

sre-marc: mitigation plan: 1) shift routing weight away from us-east-1b to us-east-2 (50% immediate) 2) cordon and drain the most affected hosts in us-east-1b 3) run NIC reset + kernel parameter bump on drained hosts 4) monitor errors and decide full AZ cutover if errors persist.

infra-joe: executing step 1 now: `rd-route update inference-main --region-prefer us-east-2 --weight 50` (dry-run then apply). Will post confirmation when applied.

maya: applying host drains on nodes with repeated RST patterns: `kubectl cordon node-123 && kubectl drain node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. expecting pod restarts into us-east-2 pool.

eng-runtime-sara: note: cache priming needed. kicking off background warmup to reduce 1st token latency after diversion. script: `for model in small medium large; do warmup --region us-east-2 --model $model & done`

support-anais: posting to status page draft: "We are investigating elevated error rate in us-east-1b impacting inference requests. Engineers are mitigating via regional reroutes. Some customers may see increased latency while routing adjusts." Can someone approve?

prod-owner-jake: approved. send now. add note we'll follow up with RCA and timeline. :thumbsup:

sre-marc: diversion applied at 03:07 UTC. monitoring: 5xx rate dropped from 32%->9% in 2m for traffic originally from us-east-1b. p95 latency rose ~120ms briefly due to warm caches.

infra-joe: started NIC soft-reset (ip link set dev eth0 down/up) and kernel tcp_retries2 bump on drained hosts. Will keep them cordoned until stable.

eng-runtime-sara: logs after reset show reduction in RST messages on those hosts. continuing to observe for 10m.

maya: triggering a canary run to validate inference flows end-to-end via diverted path. If green, we'll keep partial diversion for now and schedule full failover window if needed.

support-anais: notifying top 5 affected customers with status link and mitigation note.

sre-marc: temporary mitigation successful. lowering urgency to P2 for now but keeping page active until us-east-1b hosts fully validated. Handing off to night on-call for follow-up. @eng-oncall-nick take lead for post-mitigation verification and RCA prep.

eng-oncall-nick: taking handoff. I'll validate KV cache hit rates in us-east-1b, confirm drained hosts stay healthy after rejoin, and start draft RCA notes. pls attach any logs to the incident ticket.

maya: adding quick runbook pointer: https://redwood.runbooks/inference-az-failover (runbook: verify cache, reroute, customer notify).

sre-marc: final notes: measured customer error reduction after diversion, some sustained latency increase during warmup. Key follow-ups: full host firmware NIC health check, ANS route policy review to allow faster cutover, and adding an automated cold-cache warmup job after cross-AZ failovers.

incident-bot: Incident 1767777000 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Owner: eng-oncall-nick. Postmortem link will be created in 72h. :white_check_mark:"
